### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **30** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/default-organization-invariant.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**22** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec749fbb44b5e6015d3f205c63dfa47cfb6ef445`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/default-organization-invariant.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 34 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **51** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec749fbb44b5e6015d3f205c63dfa47cfb6ef445` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `36b13634f5a9a9c7f4257a13997c5a7e2c8b265f` — the merge of head `eb9605968ec4cb423d08c29a7931f468a02b3da8` into base `ec749fbb44b5e6015d3f205c63dfa47cfb6ef445`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 36b13634f5a9a9c7f4257a13997c5a7e2c8b265f && git checkout 36b13634f5a9a9c7f4257a13997c5a7e2c8b265f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin ec749fbb44b5e6015d3f205c63dfa47cfb6ef445 eb9605968ec4cb423d08c29a7931f468a02b3da8 && git checkout -B drift-repro ec749fbb44b5e6015d3f205c63dfa47cfb6ef445 && git merge --no-ff eb9605968ec4cb423d08c29a7931f468a02b3da8

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json ec749fbb44b5e6015d3f205c63dfa47cfb6ef445
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs ec749fbb44b5e6015d3f205c63dfa47cfb6ef445` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — REWORK (patch round 1)

`domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_01SYEJqDL3NXxrJRBVqaMu9T` · 2026-10-18T12:37Z · on head `a91dad2d8` · #24282 leg A (claim `6248532332`, report `6249921017`). This is the seat's own review at the default tier, owed for `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (`@objectstack/plugin-auth` exports `ensureDefaultOrganizationExists`), read against GitHub, not the report.

**Accepted as it stands:**
- The guard judges in its own `start()`, ordered after the engine and `com.objectstack.platform-objects`. `AppPlugin`, `AuthPlugin` and the identity-objects plugin name it in `optionalDependencies`, so a refused boot writes no row. The refusal reaches `os serve` / `os dev` down the `cause` chain (`serve.ts`, depth 8).
- With no table left in the v17 shape, an unverified marker refuses, and an absent marker boots (ADR-0131 D10 item 5).
- The ceremony creates the Default Organization only under `single` on a database that holds none, through plugin-auth's boot invariant (D3: one producer of the row). The plan says so in a warning before the first write (the 2026-10-16 amendment).
- A checkpointed `attribution` runs again only when the plan derives an owner for rows still NULL, and writes only where `organization_id` is NULL.
- The widening is one entry export (221 → 222 names), and the `minor` changeset names it. The runtime entry is unchanged. The cross-lane declaration for `plugin-auth` is #6021 `6249475347`.
- Size: 19 files, +1096 / −101. `check-governed-merges --pr 24325`: NOT governed, under the 3,000-line threshold.

**Owed in this PR:**

1. **CI is red: `Lint · docs & code guards` → `Init-service declaration guard`** (job `117675069970`). The guard reports `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts:710` (`AppPlugin`): "init() resolves getService('objectql') … and NOTHING declares that ordering."
   - Cause: the checker reads `optionalDependencies` only as an array of string literals (`scripts/check-init-service-contract.mjs:163`–`:169`, `if (!ts.isStringLiteralLike(el)) return undefined`). The new identifier element `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_BOOT_GUARD_PLUGIN_NAME` makes it read the whole array as undeclared, `'com.objectstack.engine.objectql'` included.
   - Ask: spell the guard's name as a string literal in `AppPlugin.optionalDependencies`, as `AuthPlugin` and the identity-objects plugin already do. ⛔ The checker is not edited.
   - The family is a declared wide-population one, so `dispatch-gates --commands` does not list it. Run the declared-wide families that read the changed packages (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` over the changed paths, without `--commands`), `pnpm check:init-service-contract` among them, and cite their exit codes.
2. **The ceremony and the boot define the Default Organization differently.** This PR adds a refusal for an unverified marker, which turns that difference into a refused boot.
   - The plan finds it by `slug = 'default'` only (`packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-plan.ts:1297`–`:1305`).
   - The boot invariant this PR now exports takes the sole organization, whatever its slug, when none has `slug = 'default'` (`default-organization-invariant.ts`, the find half: "The organization a `single` install derives every owner from").
   - Consequence: a 17.x `single` database whose only organization has another slug keeps its no-anchor rows NULL through the ceremony. The post-check then leaves `verified_at` NULL, and with this PR the next boot is refused, although v18 would derive every owner from that organization. That is inside A1 as the card states it ("leaves no NULL-organization row on a single-posture database").
   - Ruling (the meta-rule for one operation with two implementations: the boot's governed producer wins): the plan names the Default Organization the way the invariant does. That means `slug = 'default'`, else the sole organization. Several organizations with none `default` stays "no Default Organization", reported as today.
   - Hold the two definitions together with a pin over the same fixtures: `default` present, a sole organization with another slug, two with none `default`, and none at all. The plan file's `defaultOrganization.slug` stops being `'default'`-only. Say so in the changeset if the plan's JSON shape is published.
   - Premise, falsifiable: the find half reads as quoted above, and no ADR-0131 text limits the Default Organization to `slug = 'default'`. If either fails, stop and report with the quote. ⛔ Do not pick a side silently.
   - Acceptance note 3 then leaves the PR's Acceptance notes.
3. **Measure; change code only if it fails.** The guard now reads `sys_migration` on every served boot, and a throwing read refuses. Cite the test that shows a fresh database served by `os serve` reads the marker as `absent`, not `unreadable`, or add one beside the kernel test.

**Out-of-scope notes, settled:**
- The `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_MIGRATION_ID` docblock stays as is (Acceptance notes). It says the runtime refuses a v17-shape database while the marker is unverified. That is still true; it is not exhaustive and not made false.
- The NULL `admin_full_access` grant from a `single` development boot is dropped as covered. #15204 (C3, `pm:dispatched`) absorbs #11978 ("stop minting org-less rows") under ADR-0131 D5, and D5 states the interim verbatim: "until then the `single` row carries the NULL organization it carries today, and D10's migration is what clears it." Nothing is filed.

**Before pushing:** read this head's `Test Core` shards, which were still running at this stamp, and fold any red into the same round. The landing waits on the patch head and every check on it.

## 席位核对

ACCEPT · `domain:cli` seat 1 (seat post #6024) · `zhuangjianguo` · session `session_01SYEJqDL3NXxrJRBVqaMu9T` · 2026-10-18T13:36Z · on head `eb9605968` · #24282 leg A (claim `6248532332`, reports `6249921017` and `6250537902`). This is the seat's own review at the default tier. It is the review of record owed for `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, read against GitHub, not the report.

1. **Shape:**
   - Draft against `main`. The first line is `Fixes #24282`, with no other closing keyword; leg B is its own card, #24301.
   - `Clause-②: yes (widening)` is line-initial and bare, in the body and in the changeset.
   - Assignee `zhuangjianguo`. 19 files, +1242 / −115.
   - `check-governed-merges --pr 24325`: NOT governed, under 3,000.
2. **Premise, measured:** the card's A1–A4 path was reproduced on `d537a318b` with the real commands on one SQLite file, then re-run on the head.
   - On `d537a318b`: 10 unattributable rows; attribution checkpointed `done` at 0; the refused boot created the organization and stamped seeded rows; `verified_at` stayed NULL; and the next boot served.
   - On the head: 10 rows attributed; the refused boot moved no row count; the ceremony verified with blocking 0; and the next boot served.
3. **Patch round 1 (`6250003464`), each item read on the diff `a91dad2d8..eb9605968`:**
   - `AppPlugin.optionalDependencies` spells the guard's name as a literal. `check:init-service-contract` was reproduced red, then shown at exit 0. The checker is untouched.
   - The plan names the Default Organization as the boot invariant does: `slug = 'default'`, else the sole organization; several with none `default` name none.
     - Its basis is ADR-0093 D3, quoted: "or the sole org row if a deployment renamed it". ADR-0131 contains no `slug` text.
     - A pin holds the plan and the invariant together over one fixture set. Reverting to slug-only turns 3 cases red.
   - A fresh database reads the marker as `absent`, and the kernel test asserts it.
   - The `Test Core` 3/6 and 4/6 reds on `a91dad2d8` were folded into the round. Four storage-less `os serve` tests were refused because the engine's "No driver available for sys_migration" was read as an unreadable marker.
     - The fix: a ledger no driver serves is `absent`, as the column probe already skips an object no driver serves.
     - It widens no admission. `absent` boots only when no table is left in the v17 shape; with such a table, an absent marker still refuses. A store that serves the ledger and fails its read is still `unreadable`, so it refuses.
4. **Clause-② review of record (the widening):**
   - The widening is one entry export of `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `ensureDefaultOrganizationExists` (221 → 222 names), with a `minor` changeset. The runtime entry is byte-identical to `main`.
   - Its one caller is the ceremony. It needs the Default Organization's own producer (ADR-0131 D3: "exists before the first write that needs an owner"; D10 fate 3), and the boot that would create it is the one the guard now refuses before any plugin writes.
   - The alternative was a second producer of that row, which is the shape the one-definition item above removes. The docblocks state that no host composing a kernel calls it.
   - Accepted. Cross-lane: #6021 `6249475347`.
5. **Gates:**
   - Locally: 80 derived commands, 0 NOT-MEASURED. The declared-wide families were run as well, including `check:init-service-contract` (red reproduced, then 0). eslint over the changed files exits 0.
   - CI on this head at this stamp: 13 success, 8 roster-shaped skips, 17 `in_progress`, 0 failure.
   - ⛔ Not ready until every check on the head is green.
6. **Deviations accepted:**
   - files outside the listed surface, each named: the guard's producer in `packages/runtime`, plugin-auth (declared on #6021), the dogfood refusal-order test, and one docblock in `dev-organization-ownership-upgrade.ts`;
   - the folded storage-less fix;
   - the worktree recreated from the branch, with no history rewritten;
   - one `main` merge in round 0.
7. **Out of scope:**
   - The NULL `admin_full_access` grant: dropped, covered by #15204 (ADR-0131 D5's stated interim).
   - The `ORGANIZATION_OWNERSHIP_MIGRATION_ID` docblock: Acceptance notes. It is still true, though not exhaustive.
   - Nothing is filed.
8. **Behaviour change a host sees:** the refusal now arrives as the `cause` of the kernel's start-failure error. `os serve` and `os dev` walk the chain, and the changeset says so.
9. **Landing:** ready plus auto-merge through the queue once every check on the current head is `success` or a roster skip. #24282 closes on `Fixes`, and #24301 (leg B) stays open as its own card.
